verdict_reason: Moving from YELLOW to GREEN: the kernels are faithful and the promotion is provably clean. Analytic anchors on L = 0.5*sum(lambda_i*theta_i^2): lambda_c recovers the exact curvature to <= 0.48% for lambda in {1, 4, 100, 1e4} and for the multi-eigenvalue cases {1,10} and {0.5,3,17} (residual is the bisect_iters = 6 resolution, 2^-6 = 1.6%), and _sam_sharpness matches the closed form at relative error 0.00e+00. PyHessian 0.1 re-run head-to-head this round on the same gpt2 last-layer parameters and batch: BLME's power iteration at 100 steps gives 7.558498 against PyHessian's eigenvalues(maxIter=100, tol=1e-6) = 7.558554, rel -7.4e-6. The restore is exact -- buffers changed 0/2 on pythia-160m and 0/0 on gpt2 in bf16, fp16 and fp32; parameters changed 0/148 and bit-identical; the model's own NLL is bit-identical before and after (pythia-160m bf16 5.6783447265625 -> 5.6783447265625, gpt2 fp32 5.16782808303833 -> 5.16782808303833). The promotion removes the arithmetic bias ENTIRELY, which I isolated with an ablation: critical_sharpness from a bf16-STORED model is bit-identical to the value from bf16-ROUNDED weights held in float32 (gpt2 2.135997619162655 both ways; pythia-160m 57.21267039001523 both ways), so the residual -6.77% / +0.89% against true fp32 is pure checkpoint rounding, not arithmetic. fp16 matches true fp32 to 2.7e-4 rel on gpt2 and bit-exactly on pythia-160m. The eta0 floor is benign and load-bearing: it only sets where the search starts (both halving and doubling branches exist), and lowering eta0 to 1e-12 makes lambda_c NaN for lambda = 1 and lambda = 100 because 30 doublings from 1e-12 only reach 1.07e-3.
comparable_reason: Three of the five numeric outputs are still computed in the model's storage dtype, and core.py forces bf16 for this task, so the zoo carries a storage-format term. Measured on gpt2 (fp32 / bf16 / fp16): hutchinson_trace_estimate 112.42 / 164.7 (+46%) / NaN; top_eigenvalue_estimate 7.386 / 42.25 (5.7x) / NaN; sam_sharpness 0.07593 / 0.0625 (-18%) / 0.0703. pythia-160m: trace -106182 / -1907917 (18x); top_eig -154608 / -1531904 (9.9x). Those two also split by architecture family rather than by size (GPT-2 O(10^2), Pythia O(10^5)) and flip sign. critical_sharpness is now the one comparable member of the family, up to the irreducible bf16 rounding term (-6.8% gpt2, +0.9% pythia-160m). n_params is emitted unprefixed and equals 12*d_model^2 for the default last_layer scope -- a literal d_model^2 column.
github_repo: amirgholami/PyHessian (pip PyHessian 0.1); google-research/sam; Kalra et al. arXiv:2601.16979
github_reason: PyHessian 0.1 executed this round against BLME's own _hvp/_power_iteration_top_eigenvalue on identical gpt2 last-layer parameters and the task's own 2-sequence batch: PyHessian eigenvalues(maxIter=100, tol=1e-6) = 7.558554, BLME at 100 iterations 7.558498 (rel -7.44e-6), BLME at the shipped n_power_iter = 8 gives 7.132759 (rel -5.63e-2, a convergence-budget shortfall, not a kernel disagreement). PyHessian trace(maxIter=100) = 110.335 against BLME's 5-probe Hutchinson 112.42 (+1.9%). SAM follows Foret et al.'s L(theta + rho*g/||g||) - L(theta) and is exact against the quadratic closed form. The critical-step probe has no released reference; Kalra et al. define eta_c = inf{eta > 0 : L(theta - eta*Delta) > L(theta)} with lambda_c = 2/eta_c, and BLME's Delta = g is the documented gradient-descent specialization, exact for a quadratic (theta' = (1 - eta*lambda)theta => eta* = 2/lambda), which I verified numerically above.
paper_reason: Foret et al. publish generalization gaps rather than sharpness values for a pretrained LM; PyHessian's published eigenvalues and traces are ResNet/CIFAR checkpoints not reproducible here; Kalra et al. report lambda_c as dynamics curves, not tabulated values for named checkpoints. No published scalar exists for this quantity, so the anchors are the released code (above) and the analytic quadratic eta* = 2/lambda.
confounds_reason: n_params is emitted unprefixed and is 12*d_model^2 to within 0.2% at the default last_layer scope. hutchinson_trace_estimate and top_eigenvalue_estimate separate by architecture family and dtype rather than by any capability-relevant property (gpt2 fp32 112.4 / 7.39 against pythia-160m fp32 -106182 / -154608). sam_sharpness carries rho = +0.656 with vocab_size over 49 archived models. critical_sharpness and critical_step_size are absent from the archived snapshot, so their cross-model behaviour is untested at scale; the residual bf16 rounding term (-6.8% to +0.9% on the two models I measured) is a storage-format artifact that will still separate families whose checkpoints ship in different precisions.
defects: CODE: the float32 promotion is scoped only to the critical-sharpness block. hutchinson_trace_estimate, top_eigenvalue_estimate and sam_sharpness are still computed in the storage dtype, so under the shipped bf16 they carry 5.7x-18x errors (gpt2 top_eig 42.25 vs 7.386; pythia-160m trace -1.91e6 vs -1.06e5) and go NaN in fp16. CODE: the two search branches return different estimators of the same quantity. The doubling branch returns the bisection MIDPOINT while the halving branch returns `lo` (the last stable step).
